newsitem.title: UK: Japanese stocks in London slightly up, trade thin.
newsitem.headline: Japanese stocks in London slightly up, trade thin.

text.p: Japanese shares were steady to slightly firmer in light trade on Wednesday as investors continued to fret about Wall Street's recent volatility, dealers said.
"It's been very quiet. People just don't want to do much with the Dow looking like its going to fall out of bed," one dealer said.
In Tokyo on Wednesday, the Nikkei 225-share index climbed 167.71 points to 18,037.30, helped by a rally in major steel makers and chip-related stocks, dealers said.

Sumitomo Metal Mining was the main feature in an otherwise subdued market. After the Tokyo close, the company said it expected pre-tax profits would increase by 27 percent to 16.5 billion yen in the year through March 1998 from an estimated 13 billion yen for fiscal 1996.
The shares, which fell 14 yen to close at 724 yen in Tokyo on Wednesday, were trading at 733.5 yen in London by 1425 GMT.
